label: paragraph_title
text: COAL CRISIS.

label: text
text: DEBATE ON EIGHT-HOURS' DAY BILE.

label: text
text: SIR J. SIMON OPPOSED.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons Sir A. Steel Multland, Minister of Labour, moved the second reading of the Coal Mines Bill dealing with hours. Amid Labourite interruptions and irational laughter he emphasised the permissive and temporary character of the Bill, and repudiated the suggestion that it was part of a general Government attack on hours and wages.

label: text
text: Mr. Stephen Walsh (Labourite, Inee) moved the rejection

label: text
text: of the BiP as "aiding and abetting the employers demand for an extension of the miners' hours, aggravating the difficulties of the industry, calculated to embitter and prolong the existing dispute, and as directly contrary to the Royal Commission's recommendations."

label: text
text: Sir John Simon (Liberal, Spen Valley) opposed the Bill. He urged the Government to legislate boldly on the lines of the Royal Commission's report.

label: text
text: Several Labourites asserted that the result of the Bill would be increased working hours in coal mines abroad.

label: text
text: The debate was adjourned at Tuesday. — Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Y.M.C.A. YAPP.

label: paragraph_title
text: IMPRESSIONS OF THE FAR EAST.

label: text
text: London, juné 28.

label: text
text: On his return from his world tour, Sir Arthur Yapp, Chairman of the Y.M.C.A., said that he was tremendously impressed by the "development in the Far East, especially in Japan, and said it was an object lesson to see the up-to-dateness of cities like Shanghai and Tokyo.

label: text
text: They were infinitely ahead of us as regards electrical development, while a more gratifying note was the intense thirst for knowledge by the young.

label: text
text: He added his admiration for Japanese knowledge, and endorsed the brilliant medical man "who told me Japan was better served regarding research work than Britain, America and Germany put together."—Reuter.

text: FRENCH FLIGHT.

label: text
text:
Paris, June 28.
The airmen brothers Arnehart who departed from Paris, landed at Basrah after a 26 hours, 30 minutes non-stop flight.—Havas. Records Compared.

label: text
text: It is reported from Basra that Captain Arrachart and his brother, Sergeant-Major Arrachart, in attempting to beat the record for a non-stop flight, left Lebourget at 5:30 a.m. yesterday and landed at Basra, 2,734 miles distant, to-day. They were in the air 20½ hours.

label: text
text: The previous records was held by Captain Arrachart and M. Lemaitre in February, 1925, when they flew 2,268 miles in 25 hours.—Router.

label: text

label: text
text: Teheran, June 18.

label: text
text: The recently appointed Under-Secretary of Finance was shot dead at the Ministry of Finance by the late Finance Agent at Yspahan, who had been summoned to Teheran on a charge of embezzlement. The murderer committed suicide.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: KIDNAPPED.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHURCH WORKER LURED AWAY.

label: text
text: HELD FOR RANSOM.

label: text
text:
Douglas, Arizona, June 28.
Mrs. Aimee Semple McPherson, evangelist of Los Angeles, who has been missing since May 18, was found to-day in a hospital here by William McCafferty, editor of the "Douglas Dispatch," who had known her in former years. Mrs. McPherson was identified over the telephone after a conversation with her mother by Mr. McCafferty. The identification was established by a scroon Mrs. McPherson's hand. "Associated Press."

label: paragraph_title
text: Tells Her Story.

label: text
text: From a cot in the hospital where she was in an exhausted condition. Mrs. McPherson told the story of her kidnapping at Ocean Park beach, near Los Angeles. She said she was coming out of the water where she had been swimming on May 18 when she met a woman who said her baby was dying, and asked her to accompany her and her husband to pray for the child. They entered a sedan and immediately two men and a woman threw a coat over her head. A sweet odour made her unconscious and the next she knew was when lying ill on a bed.

label: text
text: Her captors told her they were holding her for $500,000 ransom from the church in Los Angeles. One of the men burned her fingers with a lighted cigar in a futile attempt to force her to answer catch questions to identify her mother, Mrs. Kennedy of Los Angeles, when they should begin negotiations for the ransom. They also threatened to give or sell her to a Mexican called Felipe if she did not answer. They threatened to cut off her hair and her scarred finger and send them to her mother in order to prove that she was being held a prisoner. The kidnappers expected to negotiate for the ransom through Mrs. Kennedy.

label: paragraph_title
text: Falls Exhausted.

label: text
text: The automobile drove a long distance, Mrs. McPherson said, to a house. She escaped yesterday and ran until she fell exhausted in the neighbourhood of a mountain 15 miles below the border in in Sónora State, Mexico. "At dusk she fell unconscious at Agua Pricta, just across the border from Douglas. After the Mexicans did not answer her calls for help an unidentified American brought her to the hospital at Douglas. When brought in she was wearing a mud-bed-graggled gingham dress. She asked that her daughter, Roberta, 14 years old, in Los Angeles be protected as she feared an attempt would be made to kidnap her. She believes her abductors, one of whom was called Steve, were planning to kidnap Mary Pickford, movie actress, who is now in Europe.

label: text
text: Los Angeles, June 23. Mrs. Minnie Kennedy, mother of Mrs. Aimee Semple McPherson who was kidnapped and taken to the Mexican border, left to-day for Douglas, Arizona to join her daughter who is now in a hospital there. On the same train Joseph Ryan, deputy district attorney of Los Angeles, departed to make an investigation of the kidnapping of Mrs. McPherson. District Attorney Keyes said Mrs. McPherson's story would be checked and the trail on which she staggered in escaping would be retraced. Mrs. Kennedy said Roberta, her 14 years old grandchild, had been followed on several occasions since her mother's disappearance and that the police had kept a close watch over her. Rolf, the ten-year-old son of Mrs. McPherson, has been living on a ranch near Winters, Yolo County. "Associated Press."

label: paragraph_title
text: MARSHALS.

label: text
text: WU AND CHANG MEET IN PEKING.

label: text
text: Poking: June 27.

label: text
text: After a brief rest at the station, Iarshal Wu Pei-fu proceeded to Vang Huai-ching's residence; accompanied by Tien Wei-chin and Hang Chi-huang.

label: text
text: At 9.30, Marshal Chang Tso-lin called on Marshal Wu, and cordial greetings were exchanged. Wu Pei-fu returned the call at eleven o'clock.

label: text
text: During the morning Wu, accompanied by Chang Hsueh-liang and Chang Tsung-chang, called on Wang Shih-chen and Chao Erh-hsun and thanked them for the valuable services rendered in connection with the organisation of the Committee of Safety which took charge of affairs in Peking prior to the appointment of Dr. Yen to the Cabinet.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chang Tso-lin:

label: paragraph_title
text: Wu Pei-fù.

label: text
text: At two this afternoon the two Marshals were the guests of honour at a reception given by Tu Hsi-kuei and other Cabinet members at Huaijentang, at which Wang Shichen, Chao Erh-hsun and other prominent people were present.

label: text
text: It is expected that Wu will return to Changhsintien this evening in order to direct military operations against the Kuominchun, while Chang will remain in Peking for a couple of days.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: LEAGUE RIFT.

label: text
text: KING ALFONSO DRAWN

label: text
text: 'aris, June 28.

label: text
text: The “Figno” has asked King Alfonso whether Spain is withdrawing from the League of Nations, King Alfonso has replied: “You may be sure that if the present state of feeling regarding the Non-Permanent Members of the Council does not change and if we do not obtain legitimate satisfaction, we will be unable to take the same interest as hitherto in the League. In the meantime we are appealing for the necessary conciliation.”—Reuter.

label: text
text: San Remo, June 28.

label: text
text: Zeky Bey has been released. The examining magistrate declared that his innocence had been established.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [A San Remo message of June 10 stated that Colonel Zeky Bey, Aide-de-Camp to the late Mehmed VI. had been arrested on a charge of the premeditated homicide of Rechad Pasha, the Sultan's physician, who was found dead with a bullet in his brain in March, 1924.]

label: text
text: Referring to the Malay States and Hongkong's contributions to the Singapore base, the "Times" recalls the Straits financial efforts towards the costs of the war, and declares that both during and since the war the eastern dependencies have given unforgettable proofs not only of strength and generous impulses, but of the solidarity of the constituent parts of the EMpiro in the most practical way.

label: text
text: The way the British Government can show their gratitude is to comply with the wishes of the donors, and proceed expeditiously with the scheme.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
London, June 28.
In the House of Commons, question time," Mr. L. M.

label: vision_footnote
text: LEOPOLD AMERIK

label: text
text: Amery, Secretary of State for the Colonies, expressed the Government's great appreciation and grateful acceptance of the Federated Malay States' gift of £2,000,000 on behalf of the Singapore Naval Base. The fine spirit prompting the action and its practical value would be appreciated everywhere in the Dominions. (Cheers). He emphasised that the offer was entirely spontaneous, and the money would come out of the general revenue of the Malay States.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [In the Federal Council on June 23, it was proposed by His Highness the Sultan of Selangor and supported by the others." Rulers in the Federation and by the Unofficial members of Council and was unanimously carried: "That this Council offer the Imperial Government the sum of £2,000,000 from the funds of the Federated Malay States Government to facilitate the Imperial Government in proceeding with the necessary portions of the scheme for the Singapore Naval Base as a whole and in the event of the offer being accepted approves of the appropriation of the aforesaid sum for the purposes set out."]

label: paragraph_title
text: JAPAN'S POPULATION.

label: text
text:
MALES OUTNUMBER THE
FEMALES LARGELY.

label: text
text:
The total population of Japan
Proper aggregates 59,736,822, of
whom 30,018,109 are males, according to the census of October last year. This is an increase of
9,773,769 over the corresponding period of 1920, approximately 750,000 a year.

label: text
text: The population of Fukui and Okinawa prefectures has slightly decreased during the last five years while other prefectures, including Hokkaido, show an increase. Tokyo prefecture leads with an increase of more than 21 per cent, for five years; Osaka prefecture is second with an increase of 18 per cent, and Aichi prefecture, third, with an 11 per cent increase.

label: text
text: As far as the population of the cities is concerned, Osaka ranks first with 2,114,804; Tokyo comes next with 1,995,567 and Nagoya, third, with 768,558. Kyoto has 679,963, Kobe 644,212 and Yokohama 405,898. The increase in Osaka's population is due to the establishment of Greater Osaka, which includes in its area neighbouring cities and villages. The recent drop in population in Tokyo and Yokohama is due to the great earthquake.
